titleEn: On a Narrow Path, One Step at a Time!

pages.text: "I'll get there first!" Dingding ran down the paddy bank to see the ducks below. Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, followed with a bamboo basket on her head.
"Don't run on the bank!" Grandma called. "I have to hurry before the ducks go inside!" Dingding's feet pounded faster.
Where the bank narrowed, one foot slipped sideways. A clod broke off and splashed into the paddy below. Dingding caught themself with both hands and barely stopped. Their heart thumped.
Grandma hurried over and helped Dingding stand. "Shall we measure how narrow this bank is?" She placed Dingding's feet side by side on it.
With both feet next to each other, the bank was full. "The bank is only as wide as your two feet. If you run, one foot may go over the edge." Grandma sang, "On a Narrow Path, One Step at a Time!"
"One, walk instead of running! Two, watch where you step! Three, stop and wait if someone comes!" Dingding placed each foot carefully. Not a bit of soil crumbled.

Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, came up driving his ducks. Dingding stopped and waited at a wide part of the bank. "On a Narrow Path, One Step at a Time!" Quacking ducks passed beside Dingding.
"Thank you! No one bumped into anyone." Mr. Ming waved. Dingding sniffed as the smell of ducks passed close by. Both feet stood side by side in the middle of the bank.
Now Dingding counted the steps whenever walking on the bank. "One, walk! Two, look ahead! Three, stop and wait!" One careful step after another brought Dingding all the way to the duck house.

Grandma put an arm around Dingding's shoulders, and they went down together. "You're so careful now." Taking one step at a time on a narrow path kept Dingding from slipping. "On a Narrow Path, One Step at a Time!"
